comment: Routes are client-side, so any path that is not a real file has to fall through to index.html or a refresh on /contact 404s. Static files are matched before rewrites, so /assets and the SVGs are unaffected.

headers.comment: Vite fingerprints every built asset, so the filename changes whenever the contents do. That makes them safe to cache forever: a repeat visit, a reload and a scroll all reuse the copy on disk and hit the network for nothing.
The logo and favicon are served from /public under fixed names, so they cannot be immutable. A day of freshness with a week of stale-while-revalidate keeps them instant without pinning an old file.

index.html is the only file that must always be revalidated. It is what points at the fingerprinted assets, so caching it would pin visitors to an old deploy. must-revalidate still allows a 304, which costs one small round trip and no download.
